information_asymmetry: Arms D/E/F carry a ~90-line specification of a language invented weeks ago. Arm C names Stan and Lean, which the model saw extensively in pretraining and needs no specification for. This is the out-of-distribution confound and prompt construction cannot remove it. Direction: against the Hamiltonian arms.

Arms D/E/F therefore have a longer prompt than arms A/A'/B. Prompt tokens are recorded per call so the difference is measured rather than assumed away. Direction: raises Hamiltonian cost, does not affect its accuracy.
Arm E receives compiler diagnostics that no other arm receives. This is the experimental condition under test (H4), not an accident, and arm D is the matched control for it.
Arm A' receives an explicit reasoning schema that arms B and C do not. A' is the control for scaffolding, so scaffolding is deliberately confounded with A' alone.

The model under test is a reasoning model: it decomposes problems internally in every arm. This compresses the A-to-A' difference and therefore inflates any A'-to-Hamiltonian difference. Direction: in favour of the Hamiltonian arms.
scoring: deterministic; no model judges any output
